title: Poverty and Humility Lead to Heaven

keywords: poverty and humility lead to heaven
full_text:
There was once a king's son who went out into the world full of thoughtful sorrow, reflecting upon the vanity of earthly pomp and the burdens of worldly crowns. Walking across lonely hills and simple meadows, he met a poor old man with silver hair sitting upon a stone, sharing a dry crust with wild birds that flocked to his weathered hand.

The prince sat beside the gentle wanderer and asked, "Father, why do you look so serene when you possess neither gold nor roof against the night?"

The old man smiled softly and answered, "My child, true wealth is not measured in jewels that rust or palaces that crumble to dust. He who walks in humility, seeks neither praise nor vanity, and opens his hand to the suffering, finds that the simplest path leads straight to heaven."

Deeply moved by the elder's peace, the prince cast aside his velvet mantle, clad himself in a plain coarse coat, and walked among the villages, nursing the sick, soothing the broken-hearted, and asking for nothing in return. When his earthly journey reached its evening, celestial light shone upon the peaceful meadow where he lay, and gentle choruses welcomed him into enduring bliss, proving that purity of spirit and quiet love outshine all the crowns of kings.
moral: A humble heart that shares even the smallest crust in love attains true peace and eternal joy.
